InventoryItem.title: InventoryItem
InventoryItem.description: Represents an item in the inventory.

id.description: Unique identifier for the inventory item.

purchaseInvoiceNumber.description: The purchase invoice number associated with the item.

vendorName.description: The name of the vendor from whom the item was purchased.

date.description: The date the item was purchased.

itemStdCode.description: The standard code of the item.

itemCategory.description: The category of the item (e.g., Vehicle Part, Spare, Accessories).

quantity.description: The quantity of the item in stock.

storageLocation.description: The location where the item is stored.

unitPrice.description: The unit price of the item.

itemStatus.description: The current status of the item (e.g., In Stock, Sold, Damaged).

salesInvoiceNumber.description: The sales invoice number associated with the item, if sold.

definition.description: Stores all inventory items. The 'inventoryItemId' is the unique identifier for each item, automatically generated.

params.name: inventoryItemId
params.description: The unique identifier for the inventory item.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to manage inventory items efficiently, ensuring security and scalability. We will store inventory items under a collection named 'inventoryItems'. Each document in this collection represents an inventory item and contains all the necessary details as defined in the 'InventoryItem' entity. This flat structure avoids nested subcollections and simplifies security rules and queries. The unique id of Inventory Item will be document id.

Authorization Independence is achieved because there is no need to check parents for authorization. Since all items are stored under one collection all rules can be applied to all items with same logic.

This design supports the required QAPs by storing all items in one collection, allowing for simple `list` operations, which will need filtering to show only items the user has the rights to see. This structure allows the application to scale without complex authorization checks slowing down read or write operations.
